_comment: Copy to generator/config/art_styles.json and make it yours. These twelve are a deliberately plain starting pool: they name a medium rather than a franchise, and each one says in render_as what the dogs themselves are made of, which is the difference between a watercolour scene and a photographic dog standing in front of one. Everything here is composed for a six-colour e-paper panel, so large readable shapes and strong value contrast, no smooth gradients and no fine repeating texture.

art_styles.style: watercolour painting with soft bleeding edges
art_styles.render_as: watercolour-painted subjects with translucent washes, visible paper grain and soft edges where colours meet. Genuinely painted, never a photograph with a watercolour filter

art_styles.style: comic book style with bold ink lines and flat colour
art_styles.render_as: comic-book characters with confident black ink outlines, flat cel colouring and halftone dot shading, like a panel from a printed comic. Ink and print, never a photographic or 3D dog dropped onto a comic background

art_styles.style: risograph print with limited spot colours and visible misregistration
art_styles.render_as: subjects built from two or three overprinted spot-colour layers with slight misregistration and coarse paper texture. Flat ink on stock, no photographic depth

art_styles.style: woodcut print with heavy carved lines
art_styles.render_as: figures carved as bold relief shapes, black ink on cream paper, with directional gouge marks doing all the shading. Two tones only, no midtones
simplified friendly figures in flat muted colour with slightly off-register printed texture, drawn with a soft crayon or litho edge rather than a clean vector line

art_styles.style: stained glass window with lead came outlines
art_styles.render_as: subjects assembled from flat panes of saturated coloured glass, every shape bounded by a thick dark lead line. Luminous and graphic, never modelled or shaded

art_styles.style: paper cut-out collage with layered shapes
art_styles.render_as: figures built from torn and cut paper in flat colours, layered with visible edges and small drop shadows between layers. Handmade collage, not a digital illustration imitating one

art_styles.style: vintage travel poster with flat bold shapes
art_styles.render_as: simplified geometric figures in four or five flat screen-printed colours, strong diagonal composition, no gradients. The look of a 1930s railway poster

art_styles.style: chalk drawing on a dark board
art_styles.render_as: figures drawn in coloured chalk on slate: soft dusty strokes, smudged edges, bright marks on a dark ground. Hand-drawn on a real board

art_styles.style: blocky voxel art built from large cubes
art_styles.render_as: creatures and scenery built from visibly chunky cubes with flat per-face shading, like a low-resolution voxel model. Cubic geometry throughout, never a smooth model with a blocky texture

art_styles.style: botanical field guide plate with fine ink hatching
art_styles.render_as: subjects drawn as a naturalist's plate: precise ink contours, restrained hatching for form, flat colour washes, plenty of cream paper around them

art_styles.style: enamel pin design with thick metal borders
art_styles.props: a plain background so the shapes read as a single object
art_styles.render_as: figures reduced to a few bold enamel colour fields separated by raised metal outlines, as if the whole scene were one hard enamel pin. Flat colour, hard edges, no shading inside a field
